question.worked_solution:
Notice that the given series is a geometric series because it is in the form
$\sum a{r}^{n}.$

The sum to infinity ${S}_{\infty }$ of a geometric series is given by the formula

$$
{S}_{\infty }=\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r},\,|r|<1,
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term and $r$ is the common ratio.

The first term is

$$
{a}_{1}=4{(\frac{3}{5})}^{1}=\frac{12}{5}.
$$

The common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{4{(\frac{3}{5})}^{2}}{4{(\frac{3}{5})}^{1}}=\frac{3}{5}.
$$

So, the sum of the series is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }4{(\frac{3}{5})}^{n} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{12}{5})}{(1-\frac{3}{5})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{12}{5})}{(\frac{2}{5})} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
